results.title: Kinkaku-ji (Rokuon-ji) Kyoto: Admission, Access & The Golden Pavilion Complete Guide - GO!GO!TOUR Japan Travel Guide
results.content:
| Item | Details |
 --- |
| Official name | Rokuon-ji (鹿苑寺) — popularly called Kinkaku-ji (金閣寺, “Golden Pavilion Temple”) |
| Location | 京都府京都市北区金閣寺町1 (Kita-ku, Kyoto) |
| School of Zen | Rinzai Zen — Shokoku-ji sect |
| Founded | 1397 CE — originally the retirement villa of Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu |
| UNESCO status | World Heritage Site (1994) — “Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto” |
| Admission | Adults ¥500 / Elementary & JHS ¥300 |
| Opening hours | 9:00 – 17:00 (open year-round) | [...] Q. How much is admission to Kinkaku-ji?  
 Adults ¥500, elementary and junior high school students ¥300. The ticket is printed as a paper ofuda (temple talisman) that doubles as a souvenir.

Q. What are the opening hours?  
 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM year-round. Unlike Kiyomizu-dera, Kinkaku-ji does not hold night viewings in any season — always plan a daytime visit. [...] Admission ¥500, open 9:00 – 17:00 year-round, no night viewings
 From Kyoto Station: bus 101 / 205 to Kinkakuji-michi + 3-minute walk
 Drivers: on-site paid parking (¥400/hr) — much easier than at Kiyomizu-dera
 Avoid crowds — arrive at 9:00 opening or after 16:00
 No interior access — the visit is a one-way walking loop around the pond
 The route is counter-clockwise, one-way — you can’t backtrack
 End at the tea house for matcha (~¥500) — the perfect closer

results.title: The Golden Pavilion (Kinkaku-ji)（金閣寺　鹿苑寺） - Real Japanese Gardens
results.content:
Bus: Take the bus 101 or 205 and get off at the stop ’Kinkaku-ji’. From Kyoto Station it takes around 40 minutes.  
Subway: Take the Karasuma line to Kitaō-ji station. From there you can take a taxi (10min) or the bus 101, 102, 204 or 205 (10 min).

View Google Map (Google Website)

### Address

 EN: 〒603-8231, Kyoto-Shi, Kita-Ku, Kinkaku-ji-Chō 1
 JP: 〒603-8361, 京都府京都市 北区 金閣寺町1 Tel: 075-461-0013

### Opening times

 March – November: 9:00 – 17:00
>

Times may change during special exhibits. [...] Kinkaku-ji (金閣寺), formally known as Rokuon-ji (鹿苑寺), is one of the most famous temples in Japan and a defining symbol of Kyoto’s cultural heritage. The sight of the golden pavilion shimmering above the mirror pond, framed by pine trees and stone islands, creates an image so striking it almost feels surreal. [...] In April/May during azalea bloom.
 End of November/ Beginning of December for autumn leaves.

, lit. 'Temple of the Golden Pavilion'), officially named Rokuon-ji (鹿苑寺; ( "Help:IPA/Japanese"), lit. 'Deer Garden Temple'), is a Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan and a tourist attraction. It is designated as a World Heritage Site, a National Special Historic Site, a National Special Landscape, and one of the 17 Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto "Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)").
